🌌 AI Idea Map · 1950 → 2026

How AI's Ideas Evolved and Converged

Every paper from the AI Research Progress Through the Years series is a dot in this 3D map, from Turing's 1950 question to 2026. Time runs up the helix, each research area has its own slice of the circle, and the glowing lines carry ideas forward into the work they made possible. Drag to spin it, click any idea to trace where it came from and what it led to, then jump to the paper's full explanation.

⭐ Core 120 ideas
Show years
Drag to rotate in any direction · scroll or pinch to zoom · click a dot
How to read the map: the dots are the paper cards from the nineteen AI Research Progress Through the Years articles, so the map shows what the series covers, not all of AI. The lines are our editorial reading of each paper's lineage: direct building blocks, methods it combined, or ideas it replaced. They come from the "What they found" and "Why it matters" sections of each card, but influence is often shared and debatable, so treat a line as "strongly influenced" rather than a formal citation graph. The research areas are broad groupings we assigned; many papers could sit in two. Dates for the multi-year articles are the paper's own year. Three papers appear twice in the series, once in each article that covers them, and are joined by a "same paper" link.
